appetite.category: Financial Risk Appetite
appetite.statement: The Council aims to operate with a financial risk between £250k – £500k. This relates primarily to the transformation activities rather than the core business areas in order to stimulate the initiatives to digitise service delivery or to achieve better, faster and cheaper service delivery more effectively delivered in partnership.

sources.quote: Financial Risk Appetite – Flexible

The Council aims to operate with a financial risk between £250k – £500k. This relates primarily to the transformation activities rather than the core business areas in order to stimulate the initiatives to digitise service delivery or to achieve better, faster and cheaper service delivery more effectively delivered in partnership.

appetite.category: Compliance Risk Appetite
appetite.statement: The Council aims to operate with a legal risk that finely balanced between flexible and open, following approved standards and practices as far as possible but also allowing for innovation, willing to engage in new areas of work, of significant public interest, and related to high value transactions.

sources.quote: Compliance Risk Appetite – Flexible/Open

The Council aims to operate with a legal risk that finely balanced between flexible and open, following approved standards and practices as far as possible but also allowing for innovation, willing to engage in new areas of work, of significant public interest, and related to high value transactions.

appetite.category: Reputation Risk appetite
appetite.statement: The Council’s reputation is one of the most important assets which employees and Councillors aim to protect to ensure there is little chance of significant repercussions. This relates primarily to the core business areas. As custodians of the public’s trust and public’s funds, even the transformational activities are delivered with sound governance arrangements in place and follow a strong and consistent corporate project management methodology. However, in the process of seeking the benefits of new ways of achieving or improving outcomes for the residents the Council is seeking an open reputational risk, with possible significant reputational damage or enhancement.

sources.quote: Reputation Risk appetite – Open

gaps.expected: The council's risk register with its registered risks and scores (CLAUDE.md calls it the Strategic Risk Register).
gaps.note: Not in any paper. The papers call it the Corporate Risk Register; the Risk Management Strategy (PDF page 28) says risk is reported to the Governance Committee as a Part II (confidential information) report. No registered risk, score or owner is printed anywhere in the four PDFs.

gaps.expected: Open or overdue agreed actions/recommendations with theme, due date and status.
gaps.note: No paper lists individual actions, recommendations, due dates or statuses. The 2024-25 appendix gives only an implementation-progress opinion for each of three follow-ups (recorded in audits). The audit plan covering report mentions monitoring reports on implementation of agreed recommendations but none is in the folder.

gaps.expected: Definitions of the opinion labels used in the completed-work appendices.
gaps.note: The labels Substantial Assurance, Reasonable Assurance, Limited Assurance, Weak, Satisfactory, Unsatisfactory and the advisory/no-opinion labels are used but not defined; only the NOTE on how the overall opinion is derived is printed.

gaps.expected: The findings, recommendations or risk themes behind each completed audit (including Contract Letting and Accounts Payable).
gaps.note: The appendices print service, audit title and opinion only. No finding, recommendation count or theme is printed for any audit.

gaps.expected: The covering reports to the two completed-work appendices.
gaps.note: Only Appendix A of each Internal Audit Plan Update Report is in the folder. The period each appendix covers is printed only as '(End of March 2025)' and '(End of December 2025)'; no start date is printed.

gaps.expected: The Internal Audit Plan 2025-28 itself: the list of planned audits, key risks, risk level, type of audit, date last reviewed, days and year for each.
gaps.note: The PDF is the 7-page covering report only. It describes Appendices A to F (Charter, Strategy, Reporting Protocol, Plan at Appendix D, Anti-Fraud Work Plan, Quality and Improvement Programme) but none of them is in the PDF, so no planned audit or 'date last reviewed' is recorded.

gaps.expected: A RAG colour for every band in Table 4.
gaps.note: Table 4 prints (Red), (Amber) and (Green) against Extreme, Medium - High and Low; no colour word is printed against Moderate, so its rag is null.

gaps.expected: Complete, unambiguous financial bands in Table 1.
gaps.note: Recorded exactly as printed: the Major cell prints '£500k £2M' with no separator, the Medium cell '£175k -500k', and the Negligible cell prints '£17.5k' with no qualifier beside it. In the plain extraction the dashes in '0.01% - 0.1%', '£17.5k - £175k' and 'Medium - High' are missing; they are present in the layout extraction, which was used.

gaps.expected: The shaded appetite levels in Table 3 and the content of the diagrams.
gaps.note: Paragraph 5.8 says shaded areas of Table 3 identify the Council's appetite levels; shading does not survive text extraction, so the levels recorded are those stated in paragraph 5.10. 'Chart 1. Three lines' and 'Graph 2 Risk Management process' are images with no extractable text.

gaps.expected: Rows, or the word 'None', under every directorate heading of each table.
